written_results: V(x)=W(log x)=int_1^x M(y)y^(-3/2)dy; H_(1/3)(log R)=int_1^R x^(-5/3)V(x)^2dx.
For integer l>=1, T_l=V(l)+2M(l)(l^(-1/2)-x^(-1/2)) retains both carried modes. The actual local remainder is bounded by (x-l)^2/(2l^(3/2)).
Weighted orthogonal projection onto span{1,x^(-1/2)} gives exact finite H=K+E, with both mode energies retained in K.
With X=2^j, m_j=2^ceil(j/8), integer blocks of width X/m_j: E_j<=X^(1/3)/(20*m_j^4)<=2^(-j/6)/20.
For all natural J: 0<=E_J<=1/[20*(1-2^(-1/6))]<1/2. This is a complement bound, NOT a bound on K_J or H.
Uniform K_J<=C is equivalent to the original one-third target and returns H_(1/3)(T)<=C+1/[20*(1-2^(-1/6))] for all real T>=0.
Exact finite moments retain closed floors, partial cells and all pre-block source. The positive 2x2 moment Gram is distinct from the indefinite reciprocal-phase kernel.
The retained block form is p^2/omega+(q-nu*p/omega)^2/s, s=tau-nu^2/omega>0. Failed numerical denominator separation rejects evaluation rather than deleting a mode.
For positive weights, G_ij=sum_(k>=max(i,j))w_k. Its Jacobi precision is sum_(i<m-1)(v_i-v_(i+1))^2/w_i+v_last^2/w_last. The boundary anchor is retained.
The constant-one coefficient sequence has the same bounded complement but unbounded retained energy. No bounded-coefficient universal supplier is accepted.
